page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-32 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The instance is configured with 32 dedicated vCPUs spanning 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, supported by 260 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and 48 KB of L1 data cache. Memory capacity totals 120 GB, providing approximately 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. The hardware platform incorporates advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX).

Synthetic and real-world benchmarks show balanced execution across common compute tasks. The server delivers strong single-core performance with a Geekbench score of 2164 and a multi-core score of 16691, both placing in the upper quartile. Compression metrics are equally strong, achieving 33.79 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression. Static web serving throughput reaches 56.29 GB/sec. Due to AMX and AVX-512 support, lightweight AI inference demonstrates high efficiency, reaching 411.9 tokens per second for text generation on a 135M parameter model. However, performance degrades significantly on large models without hardware accelerators, dropping to 2.26 tokens per second on a 70B parameter model.

The c4-standard-32 provides a predictable cost-to-performance profile for CPU-driven tasks by allocating dedicated hardware threads and balanced system memory. Notable tradeoffs include the total absence of bundled local storage, requiring external block storage for persistent data, and the lack of discrete GPUs. The configuration is best aligned with enterprise web serving, compilation pipelines, batch compression routines, caching tiers, and lightweight machine learning inference.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-32 is a general-purpose instance featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs and 120 GB of memory on the x86_64 architecture. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor running at 2.3 GHz, it features 16 physical cores, 260 MB of L3 cache, and instruction support for AVX-512 and AMX. The instance includes no bundled local storage and no discrete GPUs. In benchmark assessments, c4-standard-32 shows upper-quartile performance in Geekbench single-core and multi-core evaluations, static web serving throughput (56.29 GB/sec), and small-parameter language model inference. Standard memory bandwidth and multithreaded integer workloads place consistently within median ranges. The balanced resource allocation makes the instance efficient for multi-threaded services, web application serving, compression workloads, and microservice backends requiring dedicated CPU performance.
